source_name: Opentender.eu — Hungary portal (Government Transparency Institute / DIGIWHIST)
why_relevant: Merges TED above-threshold data with the Hungarian national portal (Közbeszerzési Hatóság) below-threshold data into structured, comparable records with buyer/supplier entities and red-flag indicators. Lets us see the same vendors below the EU threshold, which TED alone misses.

source_name: Open Contracting Partnership Data Registry — Hungary / TED publications
why_relevant: Registry describing what procurement data exists for Hungary and the EU, in what format, with what coverage and update cadence. A pointer source that reveals additional publishers and OCDS endpoints we would not find by direct search.

source_name: Government Transparency Institute (govtransparency.eu) — tools and methodology
why_relevant: Documents how the Hungarian procurement data is scraped, cleaned and entity-matched; the methodology tells us which fields are reliable and which HU-specific quirks (buyer name variants, entity IDs) must be normalised before vendor-share analysis.

source_name: Kohesio — EU Cohesion policy project and beneficiary database
why_relevant: EU-funded contract/project award database covering ERDF, CF, ESF+, JTF for 2014-2020 and 2021-2027, searchable by country and beneficiary. Hungarian digitalisation, fintech and public-sector IT projects appear with beneficiary names and amounts — an EU-level route to Hungarian buyer/vendor activity that never reaches TED.

Recipients of directly/indirectly managed EU funds, searchable by beneficiary country. Captures Hungarian entities (including banks, IT vendors, consultancies) receiving EU contracts and grants that are not in shared-management national systems.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság — Közbeszerzési Értesítő (Hungarian Public Procurement Bulletin)
why_relevant: National counterpart to TED: every domestic notice, including below-threshold awards, in Hungarian. Cross-referencing TED notice ids against the Értesítő gives the fuller Hungarian award picture and the original Hungarian buyer/vendor spellings.

source_name: EKR — Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer (Hungarian e-procurement system) notices
why_relevant: The operational system where Hungarian procedures actually run since 2018; procedure documentation, technical specifications and clarification Q&A are attached per procedure. Technical annexes are where competitor product names, HSM/terminal specs and integration requirements surface.

source_name: Támogatott Projektkereső — palyazat.gov.hu (Hungarian EU-funded project search)
why_relevant: National register of EU-funded awarded projects (Széchenyi Terv Plusz, Széchenyi 2020, RRF/Helyreállítási és Ellenállóképességi Terv), fed daily from EMIR/EUPR/IIER. Reveals which Hungarian banks, savings institutions and IT firms got EU money for digitalisation projects — strong lead generator for case studies and partnerships.

KÖFOP is the Hungarian operational programme funding public administration IT — the programme behind much state digital/payment infrastructure. Project-level base data identifies the implementing state bodies whose downstream tenders appear in TED under IT and security CPVs.

source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP) and contract award notifications
why_relevant: IFI-funded contract awards outside the EU-directive regime. EBRD finances Hungarian financial-sector and infrastructure clients; award notifications name suppliers and contract values, covering deals that never enter TED.

source_name: EU Publications Office — TED reusers workshops Q&A and eForms retrieval guides
why_relevant: Explains the eForms migration, field-level semantics and retrieval patterns. Without this, award-value and winner fields are easy to misparse across the pre-2024 TED schema and the eForms era — a correctness risk for any HU vendor-share metric.

Older Hungarian notices are still reachable via the legacy udl permalink pattern with an explicit HU language token — important for historical backfill because some archive links surface only in this form. Example found: a Hungary-Budapest information-system strategy services notice.

source_name: Commercial TED/EU tender aggregators (TendersOnTime, GlobalTenders, Apify TED scraper)
why_relevant: Secondary aggregators that sometimes surface IFI and non-TED notices in a searchable form and can act as a discovery shortcut. Low credibility as a primary record — always resolve back to the official notice before using a fact.

Highest-volume HU job board; banks (MBH, OTP, Erste, K&H, Raiffeisen, UniCredit), GIRO and IT integrators post here. Ads routinely name concrete platforms (core banking, ITSM, card/POS switch, ATM monitoring) and in-flight programmes, revealing stacks and unannounced vendor selections months early. Company profile pages (e.g. /cegek/giro-zrt/allasok) give a per-employer hiring feed.

Where international vendors (Temenos, Finastra, ACI, Backbase, Diebold Nixdorf, Worldline, Euronet) and bank group functions advertise Budapest roles. A vendor posting a Budapest delivery/implementation team is the clearest market-entry or new-contract signal; role text often names the client programme or platform. Also carries per-company job pages for each named actor.

Second-tier but broadly used HU board (Alma Career group), strong in IT and agency-posted roles; agencies post bank/vendor projects that the client will not post under its own name, which sometimes leaks the platform being implemented even when the client is anonymised.
Long-running HU job board (since 2000) with an IT/Telco category and heavy agency usage; complements profession.hu coverage and occasionally carries ads absent elsewhere.

Aggregator that indexes bank/vendor career-site ads plus board ads, so it is the cheapest single sweep for company-name queries ('Magyar Nemzeti Bank', 'GIRO', 'Diebold'); useful for discovering employers you did not know were hiring in HU, then snowballing to their own career portal.
Second aggregator with different crawl coverage; catches employer career-page ads (e.g. OTP Mobil) that never reach the main boards, and keeps them findable slightly longer.
Aggregator with per-company Budapest pages (e.g. GIRO Zrt.), convenient for building a per-employer hiring time series for the small set of HU payment infrastructure firms.

Largest HU bank and a regional acquirer/issuer; its own ATS lists the full requisition set including IT/payments roles, often earlier and in more technical detail than board ads. Named platforms and programme names in requisitions are first-party evidence of in-flight projects.

MBH is the merged Hungarian mega-bank (MKB+Takarék+Budapest Bank) running a multi-year core/IT consolidation; its requisitions (e.g. 'Rendszerszervező – ITSM rendszerek') are a direct readout of which systems are being migrated and which integrator skills are demanded.
Erste HU is an active digital-banking and card-issuing player; its dedicated ATS lists IT/payments roles that indicate platform choices and group-level programme rollouts into the HU entity.
KBC-owned HU bank; group IT programmes land here as local requisitions, a leading indicator of vendor/platform decisions taken in Brussels but delivered in Budapest.
RBI's HU subsidiary; career page covers expert and internship openings, useful for spotting payments/cards/channel programme staffing.

GIRO operates Hungary's interbank clearing and the instant payment system (AFR/GIROInstant). Its requisitions are the single highest-signal hiring source for national payment-infrastructure change: new modules, instant-payment extensions, request-to-pay, QR/deeplink schemes surface as roles long before MNB announcements.

source_name: MNB (Magyar Nemzeti Bank) recruitment portal — toborzas.mnb.hu
why_relevant: Central bank / supervisor requisitions name the directorate (e.g. Pénzügyi infrastruktúrák és pénzforgalom igazgatóság) and the analytical or oversight programme being staffed — an early indicator of regulatory initiatives (instant payments, qvik, card-scheme oversight) that will drive bank and vendor spend.

source_name: Dorsum Zrt. careers (via DreamJobs company page)
why_relevant: Dorsum is the largest Hungarian-owned capital-markets/wealth software vendor (~300 staff, BUD+Miskolc, RO/BG offices). Its hiring volume and named product/tech stacks track its bank client wins and regional expansion — a direct competitor/partner signal.
